C-REPAIR-OPENWEARSYNC-SECURE-TRANSFER.Summary: Repair the confirmed 71b84ab transfer and secret-storage defects and replace insecure network pairing with independently pinned HTTPS.
C-REPAIR-OPENWEARSYNC-SECURE-TRANSFER.Problem: Kotlin reuses a request nonce, JNI replaces plaintext chunk digests and records ciphertext lengths, Keystore failure uses a public constant key, and the network uses HTTP and an unreviewed PIN exchange. The original approved bootstrap baseline no longer matches the implemented repository.

Goals.Goal: Complete and resume actual Kotlin TransferEngine transfers through the Rust JNI library and ReceiverService with verified final bytes.
Generate fresh authentication for every request and retry; keep each encrypted block bound to its request nonce, plaintext hash and plaintext length.
Fail closed when protected credential storage or pinned receiver identity is unavailable, including UI and in-memory credentials.
Use TLS for all network endpoints with an independently supplied full SHA-256 certificate fingerprint; remove the custom X25519-EKE exchange and every HTTP downgrade.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve the original approved C-IMPLEMENT-OPENWEARSYNC-END-TO-END spec and plan unchanged and active. This is a sequential scoped repair, not concurrent execution of the original bootstrap plan.

Before initial enrollment the user must obtain the full 64-hex certificate fingerprint from the trusted PC and enter it on the watch. Never learn a trusted pin from unauthenticated status, discovery or TOFU.

A one-time PIN sent only inside independently authenticated TLS provides the T-004 alternative of offline-guessing resistance. Do not describe this as PAKE or as an independently audited application protocol.
Validate the exact certificate pin, certificate validity, service identity, permitted usage and TLS handshake signatures. No accept-all verifier, insecure fallback, redirect or empty pin.

Enrollment uses random 256-bit device secrets, an atomic one-use session, bounded session-wide guessing independent of device_id, expiry and revocation. Do not expose administrative enrollment or history over the LAN.

Replace the bespoke chunk cipher with library AES-256-GCM using request-nonce-derived per-request keys and authenticated chunk index. No secret-dependent home-grown cipher or PIN-derived long-term key.
Existing insecure identities require explicit re-pairing. Never silently reinterpret the old X25519 fingerprint as a TLS certificate pin.

Protect the Windows TLS private key with current-user DPAPI and fail closed on identity corruption; on Unix use private owner-only files. The public certificate may be read by the local desktop client.
Keep recordings, manifests, final file integrity, resource bounds and durable resume behavior. Limit changes to the affected transfer/security paths, their callers, tests and build gates.
Host JNI verification is not Android ART or physical watch acceptance. Keep hardware and release acceptance pending.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Changing Samsung recording discovery, hotspot topology or adding a mandatory phone/cloud relay.
Claiming all original product requirements or device gates are accepted.
Publishing, pushing, deploying or deleting user data.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The real Kotlin client with the built native library pairs over pinned TLS, transfers multiple encrypted chunks, commits and produces byte-identical audio on disk.
The same client survives a forced interrupted attempt and receiver restart, reconciles durable plaintext ranges, resumes and produces one correct final file.
Replayed authentication is rejected; fresh authentication succeeds; reconciliation failure prevents upload; JNI forwards the supplied plaintext SHA-256 and plaintext byte count.
Key acquisition, encryption, decryption and durable preferences failure produce no usable new pairing, no constant-key ciphertext and no false paired UI state.
Missing/wrong pins, plaintext HTTP, legacy pairing, expired/consumed enrollment sessions, wrong PIN guesses with varying device IDs, tampered blocks and revoked devices are rejected.
Rust workspace tests, real Kotlin/JNI receiver integration, JVM tests, full Android ABI/debug APK build and Desktop jar build pass or their exact limitations are reported.
GRACE repair baseline/target assertions and semantic markup are validated; original stale bootstrap assertions and physical-device gaps remain explicitly distinguished.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Regression tests fail before the corresponding fixes and pass afterward.
No production credentials or signing keys are committed; device acceptance remains pending.
